follow_ups.why_en: Headache: ask about vision and check BP (pre-eclampsia warning signs).
Severe headache is a danger sign: check BP and urine protein, ask about vision.
Vision problems: check BP, urine protein and swelling.
Swelling of face or hands: check BP and urine protein, ask about headache and vision.
Fever: measure the temperature and test for malaria.
Bleeding is a danger sign: ask about pain and check BP before referral.
Tiredness: check for anaemia and iron intake.
Pain passing urine: ask about fever and belly pain.
Reduced movement is a danger sign: ask about pain, bleeding and fluid.

items.ask_en: Any bleeding or spotting from the vagina?
Any fits or convulsions, or fainting?
Any headache, or problems seeing (blurred vision, flashing lights)?
Any fever or hot body?
Any pain in the belly?
Any difficulty breathing?
Any swelling of the face, hands or feet?
Any water or fluid leaking from the vagina?
Any vomiting? Can she keep food and water down?
Is the baby moving as usual?
When was her last menstrual period (to date the pregnancy)?

pcm: last time wey I see my period
yo: ìgbà tí mo rí nǹkan oṣù

items.ask_en: How many weeks pregnant is she?
How many times has she been pregnant, and how many births? Any problems before (bleeding, fits, caesarean, stillbirth, miscarriage)?
Any long-term illness (high blood pressure, diabetes, sickle cell, asthma, HIV)?
Any other complaints (heartburn, cramps, constipation, back pain, discharge, pain passing urine, cough)?
Measure and record the blood pressure.
Measure and record her weight.
Check her temperature if she feels hot or unwell.
Check haemoglobin (or PCV) for anaemia.
Test urine for protein.
Test for HIV and syphilis (and hepatitis B), with consent.
Test for malaria if she has fever.
Is she taking iron and folic acid every day?

items.ask_en: Is her malaria prevention (IPTp-SP) due today?
Is she up to date with tetanus–diphtheria (Td) vaccine?
Does she sleep under an insecticide-treated net?
Discuss where she will give birth and how she will get there in an emergency.

items.ask_en: Remind her of the danger signs and to come at once if any appear.
Agree the date of the next visit.

concepts.definition: Any bleeding or spotting per vagina during the current pregnancy.
Fits, seizures or convulsions.
Headache described as severe, very bad, persistent, or not relieved by usual measures. A headache without any severity qualifier is `headache`.
Blurred or dim vision, seeing spots or flashing lights, sudden loss of vision.
Reported fever or feeling hot. A measured temperature goes in vitals.
Abdominal (including epigastric) pain described as severe or very bad. Abdominal pain without a severity qualifier is `abdominal_pain`.
The baby is moving less than usual or has stopped moving.
Shortness of breath, fast or difficult breathing.
Swelling (oedema) of the face or hands, or generalised swelling. Swelling limited to the feet or ankles is `leg_oedema`.
Fluid draining or gushing from the vagina before labour.
concepts.label_en: Leaking or gush of fluid (waters breaking)

concepts.definition: Vomiting described as severe, persistent, or unable to keep food or fluids down. Ordinary morning sickness is `nausea_vomiting`.
Loss of consciousness, fainting with unresponsiveness, cannot be woken.
Very pale palms, conjunctivae or tongue noted on examination or reported.
The health worker states the woman looks very ill or is in a bad state.
Headache without a severity qualifier.
Abdominal or lower abdominal pain without a severity qualifier.
Nausea or vomiting not described as severe.
Burning feeling in the chest or upper abdomen, indigestion.
Painful cramps in the legs.
Hard or infrequent stools.
Pain in the lower back.
Pain in the pelvis or pubic area.
Swollen, visible veins, usually in the legs.
Swelling limited to the feet, ankles or legs.
Feeling dizzy or light-headed, without loss of consciousness.
Feeling tired, weak or lacking energy.
Cough of any duration.
Vaginal discharge that is itchy, smelly, coloured or otherwise abnormal.
Pain or burning when passing urine.
